links.comparator_used: Baseline prompting without chain-of-thought (standard prompt), compared with four other prompting strategies across five LLMs on a medical bias benchmark
links.outcome: Bias gap between privileged and unprivileged groups (accuracy gap in percentage points); significant bias reduction cases by McNemar test
links.effect: Average gap across all scenarios lowered by 2.4 percentage points; largest reduction 6.2 percentage points (DeepSeek-V3.1-sex); significant bias reduction in 8/15 cases, primarily by improving performance on unprivileged groups
links.tradeoff: Effectiveness and inference overhead varied substantially across models; no strategy was universally effective and some exacerbated bias. The abstract gives no chain-of-thought-specific overhead figures.
links.quote: Chain-of-thought prompting yields the largest reduction, lowering the average gap across all scenarios by 2.4 percentage points, where the largest reduction is 6.2 percentage points, obtained in the DeepSeek-V3.1-sex case.

design_hint: prompt engineering to mitigate bias (prompt guardrails)
